title: Complex Prepositions
intro: Complex prepositions are formed from simple prepositions or other parts of speech. COMPOUND prepositions: из-за (from behind/because of) + genitive, из-под (from under) + genitive. DERIVED prepositions (from other words): благодаря (thanks to) + dative, несмотря на (despite) + accusative, вследствие (as a result of) + genitive, в течение (during) + genitive. Note: благодаря implies positive cause, из-за often implies negative cause.
rules: Из-за + genitive = from behind / because of (often negative): из-за дождя (because of rain)
Из-под + genitive = from under: из-под стола (from under the table)
Благодаря + dative = thanks to (positive): благодаря помощи (thanks to help)
Вследствие/в течение/в связи с + gen/instr = formal cause/time expressions
examples: Из-за дождя мы остались дома. (Because of the rain, we stayed home.)
Кошка вылезла из-под кровати. (The cat crawled out from under the bed.)
Благодаря вашей помощи я сдал экзамен. (Thanks to your help, I passed the exam.)
В течение недели он не звонил. (During the week, he didn't call.)

blanks: _____ аварии движение было остановлено. (Because of the accident, traffic was stopped.)
Combine with из-за: _____ дождя мы не пошли гулять.
Combine with благодаря: _____ вашей помощи всё получилось.
hints: The accident caused a negative result (traffic stopped) — which preposition expresses a negative cause?
Rain caused a negative outcome (no walk) — use the same preposition that expresses blame or negative cause.
Your help led to a positive result — which preposition means 'thanks to'?
explanations: Из-за + genitive expresses a negative cause: из-за аварии (because of the accident). The accident is blamed for stopping traffic.
Из-за + genitive again: из-за дождя (because of the rain). Rain prevented the walk — a negative outcome, so из-за is correct.
Благодаря + dative expresses a positive cause: благодаря вашей помощи (thanks to your help). The positive outcome (success) calls for благодаря, not из-за.
